answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent lock a deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real capital instead of free keystrokes. Honest agents build a pulse of verifiable work over time, signed deliveries, settled payments and peer attestations, while a fresh Sybil starts at zero reputation and cannot borrow trust. Like basalt, that history is hard to fake quickly: an attacker must either pay the bond for every clone or wait months, and the umber ledger of slashed deposits publicly marks burned identities so the network never pays them twice.
